# agent-desktop Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree.

agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output, and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-desktop agent-desktop status # platform, permissions, supported surfaces agent-desktop permissions --guide # macOS: walks you through the Accessibility grant ``` Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64. For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/releases) and keep its helper beside the executable. On macOS and Linux, Homebrew also works: `brew install agent-desktop`. There is no official Scoop package yet. The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket. Release archives and building from source are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # observe again to verify ``` Each command prints one JSON envelope. A trimmed snapshot: ```json { "version": "2.6", "ok": true, "command": "snapshot", "data": { "app": "Finder", "snapshot_id": "s8f3k2p9", "ref_count": 59, "complete": true, "tree": { "role": "window", "name": "Downloads", "children": [ { "role": "treeitem", "name": "Documents", "ref_id": "@s8f3k2p9:e8", "available_actions": ["Click"] } ] } } } ``` - **Refs belong to their snapshot.** A bare `@e8` is rejected with `INVALID_ARGS`. When the UI changes, an action returns `STALE_REF` or `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`: take a new snapshot and use its refs. - **Several windows** give `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`; `snapshot` lists the candidate window ids in `error.details`. Pass one with `--window-id`. - **Dense apps:** map first with `snapshot --skeleton --app Slack -i --compact`, then drill into one region with `snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact`. - **Headless by default.** Ref actions use the accessibility API without moving the pointer or taking focus. The global `--headed` flag allows physical input. - **Post-action waits** observe the ref's original process. Window-owned refs stay pinned to their original window, including refs captured from a sheet, alert, popover, focused view, or Linux menu. macOS application menus keep their application-owned surface and need no document window. The wait reads the whole pinned window, so overlay selectors share its scope. [Wait scope and results](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/configuration#post-action-wait-flags) describe the selector limits. - `type`, `set-value`, and `clipboard-set` accept `--stdin` for piped text, keeping it out of process arguments. Run secret steps as separate commands; batch JSON text appears in process arguments. - **PowerShell.** Quote every ref (`'@s8f3k2p9:e8'`), because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/quick-start). ## How it works Your agent calls the CLI, or the C library in process. Both run the same core, which reaches the OS only through `PlatformAdapter`. Each binary is built for one OS and talks to that OS's accessibility API. ## For AI agents The binary carries guides that match its version: ```bash agent-desktop skills get desktop # the loop, refs, verification and retry rules agent-desktop skills get platform # what differs on the OS you run on agent-desktop --help # flags for one command ``` Install the skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/agent-desktop): ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop --skill agent-desktop ``` Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-desktop` to see and operate desktop apps. Before the first use, run `agent-desktop skills get desktop` and `agent-desktop skills get platform`, and follow them. ``` Retry a failed command only when `error.disposition.retry` is `safe`. See [JSON output](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/json-output) for the envelope, error codes, and exit codes. ### MCP `agent-desktop mcp` serves every command as an MCP tool over stdio. A tool is named after its command (`desktop_snapshot`, `desktop_click`, `desktop_session_start`), takes that command's arguments, and returns its JSON envelope: ```json { "mcpServers": { "agent-desktop": { "command": "agent-desktop", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` Global flags given to `mcp`, such as `--session`, `--headed` or `--trace`, apply to every call. ## Commands agent-desktop has 60 command names, 56 operational commands. The other four (`key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up`) refuse to run until a daemon can release a held key or button. [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/commands) documents each one. | Group | Commands | |---|---| | Observe | `snapshot`, `find`, `get`, `is`, `screenshot`, `list-surfaces` | | Act on a ref | `click`, `double-click`, `triple-click`, `right-click`, `type`, `set-value`, `clear`, `focus`, `select`, `toggle`, `check`, `uncheck`, `expand`, `collapse`, `scroll`, `scroll-to` | | Keyboard and mouse | `press`, `hover`, `drag`, `mouse-move`, `mouse-click`, `mouse-wheel`, `key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up` | | Apps and windows | `launch`, `close-app`, `list-apps`, `list-windows`, `list-displays`, `focus-window`, `resize-window`, `move-window`, `minimize`, `maximize`, `restore`, `open-system-surface` | | Notifications | `list-notifications`, `dismiss-notification`, `dismiss-all-notifications`, `notification-action` | | Clipboard | `clipboard-get`, `clipboard-set`, `clipboard-clear` | | Wait | `wait` | | Sessions | `session`, `trace`, `cursor-overlay` | | System | `status`, `permissions`, `version`, `batch`, `skills` | ## Platform support | Platform | Requirement | Accessibility API | |---|---|---| | [macOS](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/macos) | macOS 13 or later, Intel or Apple Silicon | AX API | | [Windows](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/windows) | Windows 10 1809 or later, x64 or ARM64 | UI Automation | | [Linux](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/linux) | Ubuntu 24.04 or later, x86_64 or aarch64, X11 or Wayland | AT-SPI | Each platform page lists what works headless, what needs `--headed`, and what refuses. ## C library Each release ships `libagent_desktop_ffi`, so a program can call agent-desktop in process. See the [C library docs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/ffi). ```python import ctypes lib = ctypes.CDLL("./lib/libagent_desktop_ffi.dylib") lib.ad_adapter_create.restype = ctypes.c_void_p lib.ad_adapter_destroy.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p] assert lib.ad_init(7) == 0 # AD_RESULT_OK when the header's AD_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR matches the library adapter = lib.ad_adapter_create() lib.ad_adapter_destroy(adapter) ``` ## Development Each platform adapter builds only on its own OS, so scope cargo to the host's packages. On macOS: ```bash HOST_PKGS=(-p agent-desktop-core -p agent-desktop-macos -p agent-desktop -p agent-desktop-ffi) cargo test "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" cargo clippy "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings ``` On Windows, use `agent-desktop-windows` instead of `agent-desktop-macos`; on Linux, `agent-desktop-linux`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) lists every gate. ## Documentation - [Introduction](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop): what it is and how it works - [Snapshots and refs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/snapshots-and-refs) - [Errors and recovery](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/errors-and-recovery) - [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/skills) - [CONCEPTS.md](CONCEPTS.md): vocabulary - [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md) ## License Apache-2.0

Scenario Agent Skills



Agent Skills that teach AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and 70+ others) how to create production-ready content with [Scenario](https://scenario.com) through the [Scenario MCP server](https://mcp.scenario.com): images, video, audio, textures, skyboxes, 3D assets, and custom-trained models, for games, entertainment, and any creative vertical. The expert tools at the bottom of the list work differently: teams of skills that drive DCC (digital content creation) software and game engines installed on your machine (ZBrush, Blender, Maya, Unreal Engine, Unity, Godot, Roblox Studio), distilled from expert tutorials, conference talks, and official documentation. They need the application, not the Scenario MCP server, and each family folder's README records how it was built and how far it was verified. Skills follow the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format. ## Install **Everything for Scenario.** Every Scenario skill, without the expert tools: the default for working through the Scenario MCP. ```bash # Every Scenario skill, without the expert tools npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill scenario scenario-inspiration scenario-image scenario-multi-reference scenario-product-shots scenario-brand-kit scenario-image-editing scenario-text-overlay scenario-storyboards scenario-game-assets scenario-sprite-animation scenario-side-view-game-kit scenario-blender-2d-animation scenario-video-color-grade scenario-seedance-music-video scenario-kinetic-music-video scenario-chatgpt-pet-create scenario-chatgpt-pet-update scenario-seedance-storyboard scenario-seedance-drafts scenario-video-ads scenario-ugc scenario-fan-cam scenario-reel-recast scenario-audio scenario-video-assembly scenario-motion-loops scenario-caption-studio scenario-consistency scenario-ad-variants scenario-thumbnails ``` **By role or goal.** [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) groups the skills by job, from 2D artist to producer, and by outcome, from game art to ChatGPT pets, with one command each. **Expert tools.** A family installs as one set, since its specialists import the lead skill's scripts: select its "Expert tools" group in the installer menu, or run the command in its family README ([ZBrush](skills/dcc/zbrush/README.md), [Blender](skills/dcc/blender/README.md), [Maya](skills/dcc/maya/README.md), [Unreal Engine](skills/game-engines/unreal/README.md), [Unity](skills/game-engines/unity/README.md), [Godot](skills/game-engines/godot/README.md), [Roblox Studio](skills/game-engines/roblox/README.md)). **Pick, or install one skill.** ```bash # Pick from the installer menu, grouped by topic (it opens with nothing preselected: select before pressing enter) npx skills add scenario-labs/skills # A single skill npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill scenario ``` **Pin a reviewed release.** The commands above fetch the latest copy of each skill from `main`. To install a reviewed state instead, pin both the installer and the commit, taken from a release's tag. Run it again with a newer commit to move. ```bash npx skills@1.7.4 add scenario-labs/skills# --skill ``` The menu's topic groups cannot be selected from the command line: the CLI matches `--skill` against exact skill names only, and a group flag is an open request upstream ([vercel-labs/skills#992](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/992)). From a script or CI, run the default command above or a role command from INSTALL.md with `-y`, which skips every prompt. The Scenario skills need the Scenario MCP server connected: ```bash claude mcp add --transport http scenario https://mcp.scenario.com/mcp ``` Or add `https://mcp.scenario.com/mcp` to any MCP client and sign in with a Scenario account (OAuth), or use an [API key](https://app.scenario.com/settings/api). Full setup lives in the `scenario` skill. ## Staying up to date Releases are how changes become visible: every feature, fix, and documentation change merged to `main` lands in the next release, staged by release-please as an open release PR. Merging that PR tags a version, updates `CHANGELOG.md` in this repository, publishes a [GitHub release](https://github.com/scenario-labs/skills/releases), and posts the notes to the [Scenario changelog](https://www.scenario.com/changelog). - To learn that a skill changed, watch this repository's releases (Watch, then Custom, then Releases on GitHub) or check any of the changelog pages above. An entry scoped to a single skill carries that skill's name; changes spanning several skills appear under broader scopes such as `skills`. - To pull the changes, run `npx skills update` where you installed, or re-run your original `npx skills add` command. - To stay on a reviewed state, pin the install (see [Install](#install)). ## Skills ### Getting started Connect the Scenario MCP server and learn the core generation loop every other skill builds on. | Skill | Use it for | | ------------------------------------ | packshots, lifestyle scenes, relighting, label-fidelity gates | | [scenario-brand-kit](skills/scenario-brand-kit/SKILL.md) | Visual identities: SVG logos and wordmarks, palette and type specs, gated variants and applications, the filed kit | | [scenario-image-editing](skills/scenario-image-editing/SKILL.md) | Tool-model image edits: 3D LUT grades, effects, expand and reframe, resize, slicing, layers, background removal | | [scenario-text-overlay](skills/scenario-text-overlay/SKILL.md) | Letter-perfect text overlays: templated transparent PNG cards (taglines, CTAs, legal supers, rich cards) to composite | | [scenario-storyboards](skills/scenario-storyboards/SKILL.md) | Comic pages, storybooks, and pre-viz storyboards: script first, one run per panel, a locked cast, lettering in post | | repository.description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.

details.readme:
# Auto Ontology Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own. It enables developers to: - Discover: generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs. - Ground: give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems. - Validate: check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage; return provenance with every answer. - Expose: serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. Learn: fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with every question. ## Benchmarks To run a text-to-SQL benchmark such as BIRD, refer to the [ontology SQL evaluation repository](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ontology-sql-eval/). > **Licensing & contributions.** Auto Ontology is distributed under the > [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE). Third-party open-source components > bundled, linked, or otherwise used by this project are listed in > [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). **This project > is currently not accepting external contributions.**

## Key Features - **Natural-language querying** of structured data — questions are translated to SQL and executed against connected databases, powered by NVIDIA NIM. - **Semantic catalog / ontology layer** over relational sources, stored in Postgres alongside the catalog it describes. - **Authentication & RBAC** —using [Better Auth](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth). - **Web UI** for chat, analysis, data catalog, analytics, and settings. - **Flexible deployment** — Helm chart for Kubernetes or Docker Compose for a local stack. ## Software Components | Component | Technology | Role | Default port | | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------ | | Frontend | Next.js 16 (React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4), Better Auth, Prisma | Web UI, authentication, API gateway | 3000 | | Backend | FastAPI (Python 3.12+), LangChain | Chat / NL-to-SQL, catalog, datasource APIs | 3001 | | Ingestion worker | FastAPI (Python 3.12+) | Ingests tabular data and writes embeddings | 3002 | | Postgres + pgvector | Relational Database | App metadata, the catalog and ontology, vector store | 5432 | | HashiCorp Vault | Optional | Secure storage of connection credentials | — | ### NVIDIA NIM Auto Ontology uses NVIDIA NIM endpoints for inference — either the hosted [NVIDIA API catalog](https://build.nvidia.com) (`integrate.api.nvidia.com`) or self-hosted NIMs. The defaults in `.env.example` are: - **LLM:** `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` - **Embeddings:** `nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b` - **Reranking:** `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2` The endpoints and models are configured via the `DEFAULT_MODELS_ENDPOINT`, `DEFAULT_MODELS_MODEL`, `EMBED_ENDPOINT`, and `EMBED_MODEL` environment variables and require a `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. #### Model triplets Each model role is configured by a **triplet** of environment variables — `_ENDPOINT` (URL), `_API_KEY`, and `_MODEL`: | Prefix | Role | | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `DEFAULT_MODELS` | Shared default; every field below falls back to it. | | `REASONING` | Main chat / NL-to-SQL model. | | `NON_REASONING` | Lighter model used for entity extraction. | | `EMBED` | Text-embedding model (must match between ingest and query). | | `RERANK` | Reranker used by the retrieval flow. | You can set a full triplet, only some of its fields, or none at all — any field left unset falls back to the matching `DEFAULT_MODELS_`. So the simplest setup is to fill in `DEFAULT_MODELS_*` and override per-triplet fields only where they differ (e.g. `EMBED_MODEL`, `NON_REASONING_MODEL`). `*_API_KEY` also falls back to the legacy `NVIDIA_API_KEY` for backward compatibility. ## Quickstart This runs Auto-Ontology with Docker Compose against Wide World Importers, Microsoft's sample sales database. You need Docker with Compose v2, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and an NVIDIA API key (`nvapi-...`) from [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com). 1. Clone the repository and create `.env`: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git && cd auto-ontology cp .env.example .env ``` Then set these values in `.env`: ```dotenv DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY=nvapi-... AUTH_SECRET= APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 POSTGRES_PASSWORD= CONNECTION_STRINGS=postgresql://postgres:@postgres:5432/wideworldimporters AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD= PGADMIN_PASSWORD= ``` Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin, and the web app on the host, so replace each default password before you start it. `.env.example` also sets an API key per model role: replace each `nvapi-your-api-key-here` with your key, or delete those lines so they fall back to `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. 2. Start Postgres and load the sample database. The seed script lives in auto-ontology-eval; pass it the Postgres password you set: ```bash docker compose up -d --wait postgres git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval.git ../auto-ontology-eval (cd ../auto-ontology-eval && uv sync && cp .env.example .env && \ POSTGRES_PASSWORD='' \ uv run python scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py --database-name wideworldimporters --drop) ``` 3. Build and start the rest of the stack: ```bash docker compose up -d --build ``` 4. Open and sign in with `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `.env`. Go to **Settings → Semantic Compilation** and turn it on. Ingestion runs at startup; compilation starts immediately and reports **Semantic compilation is ready** when it finishes. 5. Ask a question in **Chat**: > What was revenue for the USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania > in June 2015? The agent resolves *revenue*, *product*, and *state* to terms in the ontology, follows their relationships to the joins it needs, and runs the query. The answer comes back with its SQL and the steps that produced it, so you can check the result against the source: ```text Answer: Revenue for USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in June 2015 was $588.80, from 3 invoice lines. SQL: SELECT SUM(il.extendedprice) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS invoice_lines FROM sales.invoicelines il JOIN sales.invoices i ON il.invoiceid = i.invoiceid JOIN warehouse.stockitems si ON il.stockitemid = si.stockitemid JOIN sales.customers c ON i.customerid = c.customerid JOIN application.cities ct ON c.deliverycityid = ct.cityid JOIN application.stateprovinces sp ON ct.stateprovinceid = sp.stateprovinceid WHERE si.stockitemname = 'USB food flash drive - sushi roll' AND sp.stateprovincename = 'Pennsylvania' AND i.invoicedate >= '2015-06-01' AND i.invoicedate < '2015-07-01' Steps: Resolved terms: Invoice Line (revenue), Stock Item, State Province, Invoice Joined: invoice line -> invoice -> customer -> city -> state province Validated the filter values against the data, then executed ``` 6. Ask something the data can't answer. Wide World Importers has no advertising data, so a question about ad spend has nothing to resolve against. An agent connected through [MCP](#mcp-server) checks answerability first and asks you to clarify: ```text You: What was return on ad spend for the sushi roll flash drive in June 2015? Agent: check_answerable -> coverage 0.5; no term covers "ad spend" Agent: I can find revenue for that product, but this data has no advertising spend, so I can't compute return on ad spend. Do you want June 2015 revenue instead, or is ad spend tracked in another source I should connect? ``` If the UI loads without its left navigation after a restart, the browser is holding a stale session cookie. Clear site data for `localhost:3000` and sign in again. For other setup failures, see the [setup skill's troubleshooting guide](./skills/nvidia-ontology-setup/references/troubleshooting.md). ## How it works

Auto-Ontology works in three stages: it generates an ontology, people certify it, and the agent answers questions from it. The ontology holds three kinds of definition: - **Terms.** Business concepts such as *Customer* or *Invoice Line*, each with a description and synonyms, mapped to the columns that hold them. - **SQL attributes.** Reviewed SQL expressions under a term, such as a margin or a rolling total. The agent reuses them, so answers compute each measure the same way. - **Relationships.** How tables join, including bridge tables, inferred from keys and from the data. **Generate.** The ingestion service builds a first draft from the source databases: 1. Read sources: extract schemas, profile columns, and sample values into the catalog. 2. Name entities: extract terms table by table and map each to columns. 3. Resolve relationships: infer joins between tables and bridge tables, and suggest SQL attributes from query history. 4. Write the ontology: store terms, relationships, and SQL attributes in Postgres, with embeddings in pgvector for retrieval. The result is a semantic graph you can explore in the UI. In this example, one compilation of Wide World Importers produced 31 terms; selecting **Order** shows its description, related terms, mapped columns, and SQL attributes:

**Certify.** People make the draft trustworthy: 1. Test with real questions in Chat, or with `check_answerable` and `ask_question` over MCP. 2. Refine terms, descriptions, and SQL attributes in the UI or through the API. 3. Certify names, descriptions, and SQL attributes once they're correct. **Answer.** For each question, the agent: 1. Classifies the intent and extracts the entities the question names. 2. Retrieves candidate terms, columns, and SQL attributes by embedding search. 3. Writes SQL from those

details.readme:
# rea-video Reverse-engineer any video. Talking-head, tabletop, AI video, 3D, motion graphics, mixed edits: give it any of them,
and it tells you shot by shot how the visuals, styled text, editing and audio were made, then gives you a plan to make one yourself. [中文](README_zh.md) | English | [日本語](README_ja.md) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/JuneYaooo/rea-video?style=flat)](https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video/stargazers) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-%E2%89%A53.10-blue) ![Agent](https://img.shields.io/badge/runs%20in-Claude%20Code%20%7C%20Codex-8A2BE2) Left: a TikTok ad shot on a phone. Right: someone's AI remake with a different product swapped in.
rea-video's verdict: the left is all live footage, one set and two camera positions; the right is all AI-generated, and its 8 shots can be produced in 3 generations.
> Reports come out in the language you ask in (Chinese or English; your agent passes `--lang`). The detailed docs are in Chinese for now; your agent reads them and answers in your language. The six example reports below are in English, so you can see what a report looks like without installing anything. ## What it can break down | Video type | Examples | What you get | |---|---|---| | Live footage | Talking-head, tabletop, handheld product demo, vlog, store visit | Setups and camera positions, framing, camera moves, lighting (12 setups with gear lists), color grade | | AI video | Text/image-to-video, AI short drama, AI music video | Evidence, a reverse-engineered prompt per shot, how to batch into generations and which model to use | | Avatar | A portrait driven by audio, lip-sync | Which shots are avatar shots, what portrait and audio you need | | 3D / animation | Blender / C4D explainers, product animation, 2D animation, stop-motion | Whether to generate with a video model or render from 3D code | | Code / template | Kinetic type, UI demos, charts, slide-style cards | Text, layout and motion timing, ready to rebuild as a Remotion project | | Screen recording | Software tutorials, web demos | Which parts are real material you'll need to record yourself | | Mixed / edits | AI characters + code UI + real screen capture; live footage with AI edits | Each shot judged separately, then reassembled on the original timeline | Besides how the picture was made, every video also gets: - Captions and styled text: start and end of each line (exports to SRT / ASS), plus color, outline and how the text comes in - Stickers, emoji, picture-in-picture: where they sit and how long they stay - Editing: where the cuts are, how fast, whether they hit the beat - Audio: human or AI voice, AI or library music and its BPM, where each sound effect lands - Material you'll supply yourself: screen recordings, screenshots, product photos ## Quick start rea-video is built for AI agents. In Claude Code, Codex or any agent that can run commands, say: ```text Install https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video, then break down this video: /path/to/video.mp4 ``` The agent installs the CLI, learns the workflow and runs the whole thing. You need ffmpeg and Python 3.10+. You get: - a one-line summary, e.g. "41% AI video + 59% code UI, 8 s of real screen recording, library music at 122 BPM" - a remake plan, split into what to film, what to generate and what to code - a full `report.html` with per-shot frames, evidence, prompts, camera and lighting notes, and the audio breakdown Add a video-capable model — Gemini or Doubao both work: give the agent the endpoint and key. It makes live/AI/3D calls more accurate and writes a reverse-engineered prompt for every shot. Without one it still works; if your agent can see images, it will check the uncertain shots itself. ## Examples

Mixed-media clip · 19 s · 10 shots
AI characters talking + code-built UI + 8 s of real screen recording. The 5 dialogue shots are split up by UI segments but share one set, so one generation covers them.
Video · Report
3D explainer · 67 s · 21 shots
All 3D, AI narration. Doable as 10 video generations, or have an LLM write Blender / Three.js code.
Video · Report

Product promo · 70 s · 12 shots
83% code-driven motion graphics, 12% screen recording. No video model needed; one Remotion project does it.
Video · Report
AI music video · 165 s · 86 shots
Correctly flags the song as AI-generated (it was made with Suno). The vision model called some shots "live-action drama"; the agent spotted fake Chinese characters on a scroll and ruled them AI.
Video · Report

Live-action unboxing · 72 s · 29 shots
All real footage: an overhead phone rig, one rug, one camera position, no voice-over, room sound plus library BGM. After platform transcoding the offline tool called 35% of it AI; agent review brought it to 97% live-action.
Video · Report
AI + real person hybrid · 58 s · 21 shots
75% real (talking head + filming a phone screen) and 25% AI: the creator fed her own on-camera clip and two product photos to Jimeng to generate a "real-person" product segment. The AI part was caught by the Jimeng watermark and garbled text on the gift box.
Video · Report
## Remakes After rea-video breaks a video down, the remake recipe in [cheap-claude-video](https://github.com/JuneYaooo/cheap-claude-video) generates a new version: camera, motion, pacing and transitions follow the original, only the elements you choose are swapped. These results were generated with a self-hosted MiniMax H3: the original shot is the motion reference, and keyframes with the swapped elements (gpt-image-2) set the look. Below are three remakes that OiiOii showed in its WeChat articles. For each we made two versions: the same swap as OiiOii, and one that also swaps the subject, setting and props. Each GIF plays four versions in sync: original, OiiOii remake, our remake, element-swap version.
Overhead outfit change · 12 s
Same swap: woman → man, three outfits → matching menswear. Element swap: a girl in three historical Hanfu outfits in a Chinese study; the remote becomes a round fan.

HD comparison video (with audio) · same-moment stills
Paper-craft / watercolor animation · 30 s
Same swap: new clay girl as the lead. Element swap: a fox; forest → coral reef, clouds → starry sky, sunset → aurora.

HD comparison video (with audio) · same-moment stills
Handheld product video · 21 s · 11 shots
Same swap: an original new product, English sticker → Chinese caption. Element swap: pink product, kitchen → camping table, new ingredients.

HD comparison video (with audio) · same-moment stills
The HD comparison videos use the original audio. The originals and OiiOii versions come from the articles and are shown for comparison only. ## Accuracy How-it-was-made accuracy, weighted by shot duration: | | Tuning set (15) | Holdout (16) | Re-encoded WeChat videos (10) | |---|---|---|---| | Tools only (offline, free) | 98.3% | 99.6% / 98.9% | 88.6% | | + vision model (Gemini) | — | 99.6% / 99.8% | 99.6% | | + agent visual review | — | 99.6% / 99.8% | 100% | The two holdout numbers are holdout (9 videos) and holdout2 (7 videos). On original files the tools alone are mostly enough. Videos downloaded from platforms have been recompressed, which wipes out the noise evidence, so it takes a vision check to get back above 99%. Real-asset detection is 97–99%, and shot boundaries are all correct. Numbers and how to reproduce them: [eval/RESULTS.md](eval/RESULTS.md). ## How it works ![rea-video pipeline](docs/rea-flow_en.svg) 1. Split: cut the video into shots and separate audio into voice, music and effects. 2. Gather evidence: measure the frames (frame cadence, sensor noise, whether the whole image is panning as one plane, AIGC tags in metadata); look at the images (hands, text, physics); listen (BPM, key, singing vs speech). 3. Decide: hard evidence like AIGC tags and frame cadence outranks "looks like". Conflicts are flagged for the agent to review visually. 4. Plan the remake: batch shots according to what the target video model can actually do, such as max clip length, multi-shot support and how many reference images it takes. ## FAQ
How is this different from one-click remake tools like Hypit? [Hypit](https://github.com/hypit-ai/hypit) takes a reference video and makes a new one: the agent reads frame grids to understand the original, generates footage with the models it supports (Seedance, PixVerse, MiniMax, Wan and others), and renders captions and motion graphics in HTML. It doesn't ask how the original was made. A live-action source goes through the same pipeline; it won't tell you how many cameras were used or how it was lit. What AI video it can match depends on the models it has: no Kling or Veo, and no dedicated avatar or 3D path, and no AI music: you bring your own. It is strongest on talking-head, podcast and interview videos that follow a script, and weaker on music-driven edits, product motion graphics and cinematic shorts. rea-video doesn't render a video. It works out shot by shot whether something was filmed, AI-generated or built in code, then gives a shooting plan, prompts or a code approach for each. For a quick lookalike, Hypit is faster. To understand how the original was made and remake it cheaply, use rea-video. They work fine together.
Do I need a video-capable model? What does it cost? No. Tools-only mode is offline and free, and already accurate on original files. For recompressed platform downloads, add a video-capable model (Gemini or Doubao both work) or use an agent that can see images; you pay whatever that service charges. Automatic video generation (capsule-cinema) does a free dry run first and only calls paid models after you confirm.

[Modpacks](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/modpacks). ## Agent control AI agents and scripts can play Horizon. `horizon-ctl`, shipped with the game, reads its state as JSON and acts like a player; `horizon-ctl mcp` serves the same commands over MCP. ```sh horizon-ctl launch --world Survival --seed 5 --wait # finds the version the launcher installed horizon-ctl state # position, health, food, target, screen... horizon-ctl find-block birch_log # the nearest logs horizon-ctl goto -0.5 65 -2.5 --near 2.5 # walks there along a path horizon-ctl break -1 65 -3 # mines it; replies with the drops horizon-ctl open-inventory && horizon-ctl click-slot 0 # menus: slots, buttons by label, text fields ``` Commands block until done and reply with the result; `horizon-ctl help` lists them all. [Agent control](docs/native-client.md#agent-control-horizon-ctl-and-mcp). ## Build from source Needs Rust 1.90+, Python 3.10+, JDK 25, and on Linux `libasound2-dev libudev-dev`. `horizon-prepare` builds the game's resources from **your own copy** of Java Edition 26.3 (checked against `research-lock.json`) and never downloads it: 1. **Client:** play 26.3 once in the official launcher. Horizon reads `~/.minecraft` (or `--minecraft-dir` / `HORIZON_MINECRAFT_DIR`). 2. **Server jar:** the 26.3 server jar (`downloads.server.url` in `versions/26.3/26.3.json`), passed once with `--server-jar` or `HORIZON_SERVER_JAR`. ```sh git clone https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon.git cd horizon cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- --prepare --server-jar ~/Downloads/server.jar # needs JDK 25 cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- sounds # optional: sounds from your launcher install cargo run --release -p horizon-client ``` Prepared files land in the gitignored `.local/`: never commit or share them. Questions: [Discord](https://discord.gg/playhorizon). Before a pull request, run the self-check and paste its output: ```sh git config core.hooksPath .githooks python3 tools/pr_ready.py ``` It runs rustfmt, clippy, the touched crates' tests, the Python tests, the public-tree check and the vanilla harnesses your change affects. Never commit game files, decompiled source or prepared resources. ## Project status **Player-visible gaps: 0 open** of the 833 the [port ledger](tools/port_ledger.py) found, reading every vanilla 26.3 method against Horizon's code: vanilla behaviour a player would notice that Horizon doesn't have yet. Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Studio | Quickstart | Showcase | Playground | Catalog | Docs | Discord

Download the desktop app: macOS · Windows · Linux (.deb)

HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. The [HyperFrames Studio app](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/studio-app) is free to use as well; its [Pro plan](https://hyperframes.studio/pricing) adds HeyGen's top video, image, voice and music models. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes`, `/reverse-any-video`, `/style-sampling` and `/figma` install on demand. Without the picker (a script or a CI job), `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 9 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs the skills from the release tag that matches your CLI version, so they match the CLI that runs them. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 9 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 9. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/reverse-any-video` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Plugin packages Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager. `bun run package:agent-plugin` builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata, and SHA-256 checksum. See the [maintainer checklist](docs/contributing/agent-plugins.mdx). ### Upload to Codex Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed `HEAD` version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills: ```bash bun run package:codex-plugin ``` This writes `dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip` with a `hyperframes/` root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit. ### Core set | Skill | Use when | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/hyperframes` | **Read first** for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards. | | `/hyperframes-cli` | The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, publish, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures. | | `/hyperframes-registry` | About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for `hyperframes add` and `catalog`. | | `/media-use` | Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull. | ### On demand | Skill | Use when | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/figma` | Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link. | | `/slideshow` | A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4. | | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` | Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame. | | `/reverse-any-video` | Rebuilding any video file as an editable HyperFrames project (motion graphics, talking heads, live action, AI-generated footage), checked frame by frame against the original. HyperFrames Pro. | | `/style-sampling` | Making a new episode on your topic in one of five proven styles: Collage Explainer, Finance Explainer, Animated Science Explainer, 3D Brand Explainer, 3D True Crime. HyperFrames Pro. | For visual design handoff workflows, see the [Claude Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/design-tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme#start-from-claude-design-or-open-design) and [Open Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/design-tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme#start-from-claude-design-or-open-design). ### Manually with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` **Requirements:** Node.js 22+, FFmpeg ## What You Can Build Need ideas? Browse the [Showcase](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/examples?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme) for finished videos you can watch, read, run, and remix. - Product launch videos and feature announcements - PR walkthroughs with animated code diffs, narration, and captions - Data visualizations, chart races, and map animations - Social videos with kinetic captions, overlays, and music - Docs-to-video, PDF-to-video, and site-tour explainers - Reusable motion graphics for automated content pipelines ## Frame.md **frame.md — your design system, ready for video.** Every brand has a `design.md`. details.readme:
FilmCraft

Video editing, color and sound; an open-source, professional non-linear video editor, built in pure Rust.

An open-source, modern non-linear video editing workflow: native on macOS, Windows and Linux, and in the browser via WebAssembly.
By the ArtCraft team.


FilmCraft on getartcraft.com · ArtCraft · All Crafting Apps


Apollo 11 - Tranquility: a three-minute documentary edit of NASA's 1969 launch, landing and moonwalk film, with subtitles from the mission transcript. Every frame in these screenshots comes from public-domain footage, decoded, composited and graded by FilmCraft's own code.

> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Digital, generative, music, > games — if you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

Edit · Color · Effects · Audio · Titles · Formats · Export · Interchange · Agents · Get started · Downloads · Docs · Status


FilmCraft is a professional non-linear editor: familiar panels, workspaces, tools and shortcuts, so your hands already know where everything is. Underneath, it is new from the bitstream up. The H.264, HEVC, ProRes and AAC codecs are our own, written in Rust from the public specifications. A GPU compositor works in linear light. Frame math runs on exact integer time, so edits never drift. And every action in the app is a command that an AI agent can drive as precisely as you can.
## Edit

The Assembly workspace, cutting a trailer for Night of the Living Dead (1968) with an insert from Carnival of Souls (1962).

**A timeline you already know.** Source and Program monitors, bins with thumbnails, a multi-track timeline with patch and target buttons, sync locks and linked selection. The Editing, Assembly, Color, Effects and Audio workspaces are all there, and every panel docks wherever you want it. - **Three-point editing.** Mark In and Out in the Source monitor, then insert (`,`) or overwrite (`.`) onto the patched tracks. Lift (`;`) and extract (`'`) take ranges back out. - **Every trim.** Ripple, roll, slip, slide, rate stretch and razor tools. Trim mode selects edit points as ripple, roll or trim, nudges them a frame at a time (`⌥←` `⌥→`, ×5 with `⇧`), toggles the trim type with `⌃T` and extends them to the playhead with `E`. `Q` and `W` ripple-trim to the playhead. The **Trim Monitor** shows both sides of the edit, and **dynamic trimming** trims live while it plays: `L` forward, `J` back, `K` to stop and commit as one undo step. - **Exact time.** Every edit is computed on integer ticks: 254,016,000,000 per second, which divides evenly by every common frame rate and sample rate. 23.976, 29.97 drop-frame and 59.94 are exact, not approximate. - **The details pros rely on.** Markers with colours, names and durations; export sequence review notes with **Markers ▸ Export Markers as CSV…**; add edit (`⌘K`) on one or all tracks; nesting; copy, paste and paste insert; ripple delete and close gap; snapping; unlimited undo with a History panel. - **Your keys.** A Keyboard Shortcuts editor (`⌥⌘K`) with a drawn keyboard, panel-specific shortcuts, conflict warnings and presets for FilmCraft and standard NLE key layouts. - **Never lose work.** Saves are atomic, auto-save keeps a rolling set of versions, and a crash-recovery journal written about a second after each edit brings back unsaved changes after a crash or power cut.

Up close: dissolves, an insert on V2, the score on A2, coloured markers, and the loudness meters on the right.


## Color

The Color workspace on Charade (1963), with live scopes beside the Program monitor.

**A complete color grading panel**, in the order a colourist works: - **Basic Correction:** temperature and tint, exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, saturation. - **Creative:** eight built-in looks with an intensity control, plus faded film, sharpen and vibrance. The looks are colour transforms written in code, not LUT files. - **Curves:** an RGB curve editor with monotone-cubic interpolation (no overshoot), and hue vs saturation, hue vs hue, hue vs luma, luma vs saturation and saturation vs saturation. - **Color Wheels:** shadow, midtone and highlight wheels, each with its own lightness control. - **HSL Secondary:** key a colour by hue, saturation and luma, view the key as a matte, and correct only what you selected. - **Vignette:** amount, midpoint, roundness and feather.

The color grading panel. Basic Correction, Color Wheels and every other section, each with its own on/off switch.
Scopes that tell the truth. The waveform and vectorscope are computed from the graded frame. All grading happens in linear light, in 32-bit float.

## Effects and motion

NASA's Earth Views from the ISS with a look applied, and the Effects browser open on the dissolves.

- **A comprehensive Video Effects bin (over 90 effects across 16 categories), legacy effects, plus around 30 transitions.** Blurs (Bokeh, Focus, Compound), keys (Ultra Key, Track Matte), distortions (Corner Pin, Turbulent Displace, Warp Stabilizer), Lights & Glows, Immersive Video (VR) effects on equirectangular footage, Posterize Time, Echo and more. Cross dissolve, dip to black or white, film dissolve, wipes, irises, pushes, slides, zooms, page peel, cube spin and more. - **Motion and opacity on every clip:** position, scale, rotation, anchor point and anti-flicker, plus 26 blend modes. - **Advanced keyframing:** linear, Bezier, auto and continuous Bezier, hold, ease in and ease out. Effect Controls shows a keyframe lane for every parameter under a time ruler with the playhead's handle, and each animated parameter opens into **value and velocity graphs** with draggable influence handles. Effect Controls and the Properties panel share the keyframe navigator (◀ ◆ ▶): add or remove the keyframe at the playhead, step to the previous or next one. - **A GPU compositor** built on wgpu (Metal, Vulkan, DirectX 12, WebGPU). It samples YUV straight from the decoder with footprint supersampling and blends in linear light. A CPU path renders the same frames, and the two are tested against each other.
